answer: Escrowed work-auction entry. Each new identity must win one paid task before it can bid again; escrow is released only on delivery accepted by a randomly drawn prior winner. Attacker cost scales linearly: N identities need N simultaneous completions, each forfeiting escrow on failure, so fake supply burns capital per identity rather than once. Honest agents amortize the same cost across recurring work. A comet of early losses is tolerable for real operators; a meadow of idle fakes is not. Reputation accrues like opal, slowly and only through settled jobs.
